correctness.rationale: For every dyadic modulus, expanding the cubic ambiguity reduces exactly to a quadratic Gauss sum. The primitive 2-adic Gauss-sum square is 2^(m+1) for m>=2 and only even linear coefficient; the modulus-2 sum instead survives only for odd linear coefficient. This dichotomy exhausts all valuations and yields support count (N^2+2)/3, exact magnitudes, and multiplicities. Weyl orthogonality yields lifted singular values sqrt(N)|A| without assuming any zero-free ambiguity. Standalone checks exactly verify every potential zero for N=2..128 using cyclotomic coefficient identities, plus numerical magnitudes N<=32 and Gram eigenvalues N<=8. Computations are corroboration, not infinite proof.
